## Recovered observations

170 points (40 from F5-31; 130 from F5-32) read by two readings made separately and reconciled (batch `curves-s5-b1`, rules `docs/CURVE-READING.md (2026-10-08)`). Values are SI; the printed-unit values and the pixel coordinates on the page image are kept beside them so every point can be checked against the scan. x_read_bound and y_read_bound are reading bounds in printed units: the largest change of value over the point's pixel interval on the piecewise map, plus the location error of the two lines around it (D-025; the global calibration residual is not added, see qa/<batch>/calibration-sensitivity.md for the affine difference); x_bound_si and y_bound_si are the same in SI. They are not standard deviations.

Both readings drawn on the page image (filled circles: Claude's reading; hollow squares: Codex's; bars: pixel bounds; the canonical reading of each panel is named in the batch review). Click to enlarge.

Panel 1: No. 1 footpad of the 1/6-scale model, NASA Test No. 2.
The depth is a computed output, not a direct measurement: the report's data reduction program took the 13 tape-recorded signals every 1/1000 s and calculated the footpad's penetration by numerical integration (AM-68-1 Vol. I, Section 5.5.2, printed 5-41, PDF 321).

Panel 2: Axial load of the strut, tension positive and compression negative, as the panel's printed labels give it (the axis title names the sense of the trace's main excursion); a trace beyond the panel's 0 line changes sense.
On Fig. 5-32, past 0.09 s the time is extrapolated: the 0.10 s line is too faint on the scan to anchor, and the three strut traces end at about 0.103 s in both readings.

Panel 3: Axial load of the strut, tension positive and compression negative, as the panel's printed labels give it (the axis title names the sense of the trace's main excursion); a trace beyond the panel's 0 line changes sense.
On the Strut No. 2 panel the top load label is printed -60; the panel's own sequence (0, +20, +40) and the (Tension) title make it +60, and both readings anchor that line at +60 lbf.
On Fig. 5-32, past 0.09 s the time is extrapolated: the 0.10 s line is too faint on the scan to anchor, and the three strut traces end at about 0.103 s in both readings.

Panel 4: Axial load of the strut, tension positive and compression negative, as the panel's printed labels give it (the axis title names the sense of the trace's main excursion); a trace beyond the panel's 0 line changes sense.
On Fig. 5-32, past 0.09 s the time is extrapolated: the 0.10 s line is too faint on the scan to anchor, and the three strut traces end at about 0.103 s in both readings.

Panel 2, strut3: the line is broken after claude sample 9: a break in the drawn line at about 0.0089 to 0.0091 s, about 4 px of the page with no ink; seen by the Claude reader and in Codex's review, confirmed on the page; the line is not drawn across it.

Panel 4, strut1: the line is broken after claude sample 17: a break in the drawn line at about 0.0261 to 0.0263 s, about 4 px of the page with no ink; seen by the Claude reader and in Codex's review, confirmed on the page; the line is not drawn across it.

## Notes from the two readings

- Claude: Bendix drop No. 11 (7-19-67, test type C) is NASA Test No. 2; the T5-2 remark prints NASA Drop No. 2. The F5-32 inset is a degraded scan: read Vv = -60.55 and Vh = 83.75 In. Sec. with the leading digits uncertain; T5-3 prints VV -60.5 and Vh 83.5 In./Sec., T5-2 prints 5 and 7 with no unit, text 5-44 nominal five and seven ft/s; F5-34 and F5-36 start near -60 and 84 in/s. Release to touchdown time .177 sec (T5-3). Dr 0 printed with 46.9 pcf and phi 41 (T5-2 and T5-3) whereas soil 1 RS Loose is Dr 0 at 41.4 pcf and phi 40 in Table 2-3; soil 1 mapped by state only. Loose bed depth not printed. NASA Test No. 3 (drop 12) duplicates this condition.
- Codex: NASA Test No. 2. F5-32 reads -60.55 and 83.75 in./sec. T5-3 gives -60.5 and 83.5 In./Sec. T5-2 nominal Vv 5 and Vh 7 fps. Impact-path angle not tabulated. Loose-bed fill depth, model pad diameter and run Gp unreported. Earth gravity inferred.
